note: Text for the rotation cards. Benefits are not written here: the app computes them against the rotation the user marks as current (web/js/soilwater.js versus()).

A_continuous_corn.why: The baseline: what the field gives if nothing changes. Grain corn every year is the simplest plan to run and to market.
evidence: Corn after corn keeps rootworm eggs laid this year hatching under next year's corn [MAPAQ / RAP fiche chrysomèle des racines du maïs]
Grass crops sustain wireworm populations, and corn is a grass [Saguez et al. 2017]
Grain corn has the USLE crop type factor 0.40 [OMAFRA Factsheet 23-005]
risks: Rootworm and wireworm pressure stays, so coated seed is more likely to be needed
The highest nitrogen bill of the four plans, every year
Bare soil from harvest in November to crop cover the next June
gaps: No yield penalty for corn after corn is counted; the yield is the Quebec mean for all corn

B_corn_soy_wheat.why: A three-crop rotation: a legume and a small grain break the corn cycle, and wheat covers the soil from April.
evidence: One year out of corn breaks the rootworm cycle [MAPAQ / RAP fiche chrysomèle des racines du maïs]
Soybean leaves about 25 kg N/ha to the next crop [CRAAQ 2010, cited by N'Dayegamiye et al. 2012]
Spring wheat is sown when the 10-day mean air temperature reaches 5 C, about five weeks before corn [FAO-56 Ch. 6]
Wheat straw: 1.5 t of residue per t of grain [Lal 2005]
risks: Wheat is a grass, so wireworms are not starved in the wheat year [Saguez et al. 2017]
Wheat finishes in late summer, when a dry July can cut the yield: see the dry-year shortfall
Three crops to market instead of one or two
gaps: No cover crop after wheat is counted; one would cut the bare-soil days further

C_with_buckwheat.why: Adds buckwheat, which slows wireworm larvae, before soybean and wheat: the plan aimed most directly at the pest.
evidence: Wireworm larvae survived 15 % on buckwheat against 44 % on barley over 120 days [Noronha et al. 2023]
One year out of corn breaks the rootworm cycle [MAPAQ / RAP fiche chrysomèle des racines du maïs]
risks: Buckwheat is a niche market in Quebec; the price and the buyer must be found first
Buckwheat is not a biofumigant: it slows larvae, it does not kill them [Noronha et al. 2023]
gaps: FAO-56 gives no crop coefficient for buckwheat, so its water use is not computed

D_corn_soy.why: A two-crop plan: corn and soybean in turn. Marked as the current rotation by default; mark your own.
evidence: One year out of corn breaks the rootworm cycle [MAPAQ / RAP fiche chrysomèle des racines du maïs]
Soybean leaves about 25 kg N/ha to the next corn [CRAAQ 2010, cited by N'Dayegamiye et al. 2012]
Soybean has the USLE crop type factor 0.50, higher than corn's 0.40: less residue to cover the soil [OMAFRA Factsheet 23-005]
risks: A rootworm variant in the US Corn Belt lays eggs in soybean, which undoes the one-year break; whether it is in Quebec is not checked here
Soybean leaves little residue, so the soil is barer in the soybean years
gaps: How common this rotation is in Quebec was not checked against a census figure
